en.question: When do few-shot examples deliver the most value?

options.text: When the task is simple and the instruction is already unambiguous.
options.note: Simple tasks rarely need examples; they just add tokens.

options.text: When an output format or edge-case convention is easier shown than described.
When input token count must be reduced without changing the task at all.
options.note: Examples increase input tokens rather than reducing them.

options.text: When the model needs access to private data it was not trained on.
options.note: Examples cannot supply missing data; that is retrieval's job.

en.explanation: Examples are most powerful for conveying format and conventions, especially edge cases where a prose rule would be long and ambiguous but a single demonstration is instantly clear.
